general_information.Description: This course equips students with foundational and applied knowledge of automotive electrical and electronic systems. It covers the operating principles of engine electrical systems, vehicle body electrical components, and the various electronic features integrated into modern vehicles. Students will explore the structure, functions, and operating mechanisms of Electronic Control Units (ECUs), including how they monitor, regulate, and optimize different vehicle subsystems. Through this course, learners will develop both theoretical understanding and practical insights into the electrical and electronic technologies that underpin contemporary automotive engineering.
general_information.StudentTasks: - Students must attend at least 80% of contact sessions in order to be accepted to the final examination. - Student is responsible to do all exercises, assignments and practical given by instructor in class or at home and submit on time. Do quizzes during class.
general_information.Tools: - Intenet - Textbook - AI Tools and Simulator software

learning_outcomes.CLO Details: Have knowledge of basic parts of automotive electrical and electronic systems, electrical and electronic principles
Have basic knowledge of tools and equipment used for electrical and electronics in cars
Students will learn about Batterries, Charging, Starting, Ignition, Fuel control.
Introduce further areas of engine control. Some of the main issues are,Ignition timing, Dwell angle, Fuel quantity, Exhaust gas recirculation (EGR, Canister purge, Idle speed)
Ability to design, simulate and operate and configure components in automotive electrical and electronic systems
Investigate, evaluate and communicate general trends in computing technologies such as Instruction-Level Parallelism and Superscalar Processors
Using AI tools and simulator tools to futher explore the main concepts
